a:r.a:t: As mentioned on the previous slide, there are a number of different types of neural networks. If you really want to spend more time on the details of neural networks, you can find a very detailed list of network types and what they are useful for here:

Two very common neural networks are shown on this slide. The first is known as a convolutional neural network (CNN) which is used frequently in image processing. A CNN is looking at sections of an image at a time and essentially is looking for patterns across the sets of data (lines, edges, curves, etc.). This is why CNNs excels at classifying images and detecting objects within an image (as it is looking for similar patterns across sets of data). The second common network is known as a recurrent neural network (RNN) which takes the output of some layers and uses them as input for the same layer. This is often used for text recognition because it learns from what it found in the past. For example, an RNN is a good method to know that a “dog” is different when you put the word “hot” in front of it. RNNs are also frequently used for speech recognition as it is often needed for understanding the context of a sentence (looking at the entire sentence and not just each individual word is important to understand the context).
